summary: Credential-safe error display (W8): errors show only parts built up as safe from the input. safe_location() keeps scheme, host, port and path of a URL (drops userinfo, query, fragment; a scheme without '//' becomes '***'; local paths pass through), safe_detail() shows '[Errno N] strerror' for OSError or just the exception class name, safe_cause() rebuilds an errno-only OSError or returns None, and raise_safe() raises with only that safe cause reachable and __context__ cleared. Stdlib only; must not import errors.py.
lifecycle_notes: Built up from the input rather than masked down: no driver text is ever shown, only the class name (or errno/strerror for OSError).
raise_safe clears __context__ explicitly because 'raise ... from' alone keeps the active exception there.
Behaviour mirrors the mountainash-auth-client helper; data-owned, no cross-package import.
documentation_hooks: Security note: connection errors read '{safe location|dialect}: connection failed (ExceptionType)' and never echo credentials or driver text (W8).
risks: Duplicated from the auth-client helper by design; the two copies must be kept in step.
